subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when a disabled provider is the selected primary or an explicit fallback?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds a public config option and changes provider-routing/fallback semantics that repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Approve Shared Provider Eligibility
options.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject Provider-Level Disable
options.body: Keep the current model where operators remove or edit provider/model/fallback config, avoiding another public config knob and its upgrade semantics.

options.title: Defer To Provider Lifecycle Design
options.body: Hold this until provider enablement, plugin setup, auth/status, model picker, and fallback lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve Shared Provider Eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal across model config planning, fallback, catalog, and status surfaces where this product contract would land.
